nodes.name: hcp_can_create_patient
nodes.summary: HCPs must be permitted to create patient accounts.
nodes.source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

nodes.name: hcp_cannot_view_patient_credentials
nodes.summary: HCPs must not be permitted to view a patient's password or security question.
nodes.source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

nodes.name: hcp_cannot_edit_patient_credentials
nodes.summary: HCPs must not be permitted to edit a patient's password or security question.
nodes.source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

nodes.id: property:same-action editPatientCredential permissions for HCPs on Patient resources
nodes.name: same-action editPatientCredential permissions for HCPs on Patient resources
admin_can_create_lhcp
nodes.summary: Administrators must be permitted to create LHCP accounts.
nodes.source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

nodes.name: hcp_cannot_edit_patient_mid
nodes.summary: HCPs must not be permitted to edit a patient's MID.
nodes.source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

nodes.name: admin_can_create_emergency_responder
nodes.summary: Administrators must be permitted to create emergency responder accounts.
nodes.source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

nodes.name: admin_can_create_public_health_agent
nodes.summary: Administrators must be permitted to create public health agent accounts.
nodes.source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

nodes.name: lhcp_can_create_uap
nodes.summary: LHCPs must be permitted to create UAP users.
nodes.source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

nodes.name: hcp_can_edit_non_mid_patient_data
nodes.summary: HCPs must be permitted to edit patient data fields other than the patient's MID.
nodes.source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

nodes.name: user_can_login_with_own_credentials
nodes.summary: Users must be permitted to log in to their own session when they provide their own MID and password.
nodes.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

nodes.name: login_only_with_own_credentials
nodes.summary: Users must not be permitted to log in unless they are logging in to their own session with their own MID and password.
nodes.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

nodes.name: user_can_request_own_password_change
nodes.summary: Users must be permitted to request a password change for their own user account.
nodes.source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

nodes.name: password_change_only_own_account
nodes.summary: Users must not be permitted to request a password change for any account other than their own.
nodes.source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

nodes.name: user_can_logout_own_session
nodes.summary: Users must be permitted to log out of their own authenticated session.
nodes.source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

nodes.name: logout_only_own_authenticated_session
nodes.summary: Users must not be permitted to log out any session unless it is their own authenticated session.
nodes.source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

nodes.name: user_can_close_own_authenticated_session
nodes.summary: Users must be permitted to close the application for their own authenticated session.
nodes.source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

nodes.name: close_application_only_own_authenticated_session
nodes.summary: Users must not be permitted to close the application for any session unless it is their own authenticated session.
nodes.source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the iTrust application.

nodes.name: admin_can_set_inactivity_period_length
nodes.summary: Administrators must be permitted to set the system inactivity period length.
nodes.source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

nodes.name: patient_can_view_own_past_and_designated_lhcps
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to view the LHCPs on their own record that they have visited or designated.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

nodes.name: view_past_and_designated_lhcps_only_own_patient_record
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to view past or designated LHCPs for any patient record other than their own.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

nodes.name: patient_can_add_provider_to_own_list
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to add an HCP to their own provider list.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

nodes.name: add_provider_only_to_own_list
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to add a provider to any patient provider list other than their own.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

nodes.name: patient_can_designate_lhcp_for_self
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to designate an LHCP as a DLHCP for their own patient record.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

nodes.name: designate_lhcp_only_for_own_record
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to designate an LHCP as a DLHCP for any patient record other than their own.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

nodes.name: patient_can_undesignate_lhcp_for_self
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to undesignate an LHCP as a DLHCP for their own patient record.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

nodes.name: undesignate_lhcp_only_for_own_record
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to undesignate an LHCP as a DLHCP for any patient record other than their own.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

nodes.name: patient_can_view_own_access_log_for_chosen_period
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to view their own access log for a chosen access-log period with a beginning date no later than the end date.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

nodes.name: view_access_log_only_own_log_for_valid_period
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to view an access log unless it is their own access log and the requested beginning date is no later than the end date.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

nodes.name: patient_can_view_own_medical_record_with_family_history
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to view their own medical records, including records that contain family history.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history. ... for their own records

nodes.name: personal_representative_can_view_represented_medical_record_with_family_history
nodes.summary: Personal representatives must be permitted to view medical records, including family history, for patients whom they represent.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history. ... for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: view_medical_record_only_own_or_represented_patient
nodes.summary: Patients and personal representatives must not be permitted to view a medical record unless the record belongs to the patient user or to a patient whom the personal representative represents.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history. ... for their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: patient_can_see_own_personal_health_information
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to see personal health information in their own medical records when the record contains that information category.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information ... for their own records

nodes.name: see_health_information_only_own_or_represented_valid_category
nodes.summary: Patients and personal representatives must not be permitted to see record health information unless the record is their own or for a represented patient, and the requested information category is one of the permitted categories that the record contains.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records and the records for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: patient_can_search_providers_by_named_criteria
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to search for providers using name and specialty criteria, with zip code allowed as an optional search criterion.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

nodes.name: personal_representative_can_see_represented_personal_health_information
nodes.summary: Personal representatives must be permitted to see personal health information in medical records for patients whom they represent when the record contains that information category.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information ... for ... records for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: patient_can_see_own_immunizations
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to see immunization information in their own medical records when the record contains immunizations.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records...

nodes.name: personal_representative_can_see_represented_immunizations
nodes.summary: Personal representatives must be permitted to see immunization information in medical records for patients whom they represent when the record contains immunizations.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see ... immunizations ... for ... records for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: patient_can_see_own_office_visit_information
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to see office-visit information in their own medical records when the record contains office-visit information.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records...

nodes.name: personal_representative_can_see_represented_office_visit_information
nodes.summary: Personal representatives must be permitted to see office-visit information in medical records for patients whom they represent when the record contains office-visit information.
nodes.source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see ... office visit information ... for ... records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.name: lhcp_creation_requires_specialty
nodes.summary: Administrators must not be permitted to create an LHCP unless the new LHCP has a specified specialty.
nodes.source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.

nodes.name: search_providers_only_by_named_criteria
nodes.summary: Patients must not be permitted to search for providers unless the search includes non-empty name and specialty criteria, and any supplied zip code is non-empty.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

nodes.name: patient_can_view_own_medical_record
nodes.summary: Patients must be permitted to view their own medical records.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history. ... for their own records

nodes.name: personal_representative_can_view_represented_medical_record
nodes.summary: Personal representatives must be permitted to view medical records for patients whom they represent.
nodes.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history ... for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.

nodes.reason: The atom captures a materially useful positive permission from the requirement: HCPs must be allowed to create patient accounts. The validated schema has a direct action/resource hook for this, and the source excerpt does not add an omitted ownership, lifecycle, authentication, or conflict boundary for this specific permission. Related constraints about initial fields, MID immutability, and credential secrecy should be covered by separate atoms rather than folded into this floor.

The atom captures a distinct explicit credential-secrecy boundary from the source: HCPs must not view a patient's password or security question. The validated schema has a direct action hook and context field for the credential name, so this is not merely a role/type restatement or proxy. It is not duplicated by the approved create-patient floor. Separate atoms may still be needed for enter/edit credential denial, but this view-specific atom is tightly scoped and useful.

The atom captures a distinct credential integrity prohibition from the source: HCPs must not edit a patient's password or security question. It is not redundant with the already-approved view prohibition, and the validated schema has a direct action/context hook via editPatientCredential and context.credentialField to express the named boundary tightly.

The positive HCP edit floor is materially relevant, but the source requirement includes a named field-level boundary: the patient's MID must not be editable. The proposed atom permits editPatientData for any HCP/Patient without any way to exclude MID edits. The validated schema/action lacks an edited-field or data-field context hook for editPatientData, so this cannot be repaired as a scoped property without a schema change.

The atom is a materially useful floor for an explicit source permission and is not duplicated by approved atoms or implied by the schema's appliesTo typing. The related specialty requirement is represented on the LHCP resource as a required attribute, so this creation floor is not omitting a separately expressible authorization boundary from the cited creation sentence.

The atom captures a distinct, source-explicit field-level safety boundary: HCP patient-data edits must exclude the patient's MID. The validated schema exposes the needed hook via editPatientData.context.editedField, so this is directly representable and not a proxy. It is not redundant with the approved credential atoms and repairs the earlier overly broad HCP edit proposal by scoping the disjointness to editedField == "mid".

The atom is a tightly scoped positive floor directly supported by the source sentence granting administrators the ability to create emergency responders. It is not redundant with the approved LHCP creation atom, is not implied by the schema's appliesTo typing alone, and the source excerpt does not add a further emergency-responder-specific lifecycle, ownership, network, authentication, or conflict boundary that this property omits.

The atom is a distinct, tightly scoped floor for the explicit source grant that administrators can create public health agents. It is not already covered by the approved administrator creation atoms for LHCPs or emergency responders, and the validated schema has a direct createPublicHealthAgent action with matching Administrator/PublicHealthAgent boundaries. The source excerpt does not add a narrower condition for this specific create action that the atom omits.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped to the explicit requirement that an LHCP can create UAP users. It is not already covered by approved atoms, does not merely restate schema typing because it asserts a required permission floor, and the source excerpt does not name additional ownership, lifecycle, authentication, network, or conflict boundaries for this action.

The atom is materially useful because it covers the positive HCP edit workflow that is not implied by the approved disjointness atom. It is tightly scoped to the source's named MID immutability boundary using the schema's existing editPatientData context.editedField hook, and it avoids the previously rejected broad floor that would require MID edits to be permitted.

The atom targets a real, uncovered administrative capability, but the proposed floor omits the source's named assignment boundary that the administrator chooses the hospital set for the LHCP. The validated action already exposes this as context.hospitals, so the property should be repaired to scope the floor to the requested/chosen hospital set rather than a generic Administrator/LHCP principal-resource permission.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and uses the existing context.hospitals hook, but the proposed condition context.hospitals == resource.hospitals is not the named source boundary. It over-constrains the floor to cases where the requested hospital set already equals the LHCP's current hospital set, which can collapse the assignment capability into a no-op and does not express the administrator's ability to choose the hospitals to assign. Repair the atom to cover administrator assignment for the requested/chosen context.hospitals set without requiring equality to the pre-existing resource.hospitals.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement, and the schema exposes the named boundary as context.hospitals. However, the proposed reference Cedar still only states the Administrator/LHCP principal-resource floor and does not explicitly bind the permission to the requested/chosen hospital set. Because prior rejected variants specifically required using the existing context.hospitals hook rather than a generic assignment floor, this should be repaired to make the chosen/requested hospitals boundary explicit without requiring equality to resource.hospitals.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped to the source requirement. It is not a generic User/Session floor: it uses the schema-exposed session ownership and credential hooks to capture the named boundary that the user enters their own MID and password. It is not duplicative of approved atoms and does not omit an expressible source boundary for this login capability.

The atom is materially useful as a safety ceiling distinct from the already-approved login floor. It captures the source's credential ownership boundary by requiring the entered MID and password to match the principal's own attributes, and it also uses the schema's Session.user hook to prevent logging into another user's session. It is not merely a principal/resource type restatement and is not implied by the approved floor.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and correctly avoids the prior overconstraint requiring context.hospitals to equal resource.hospitals. However, the proposed reference Cedar condition `context.hospitals == context.hospitals` is tautological, so the property still collapses to a generic Administrator/LHCP assignment floor and does not materially bind the permission to the chosen/requested hospital set. Repair the atom to make the existing `context.hospitals` assignment payload explicit as the hospital set being authorized, without using a tautology or requiring equality to the LHCP's current hospitals.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and uses the existing context.hospitals hook, but the added condition context.hospitals != resource.hospitals is an invented boundary not present in the source. It over-constrains the floor by requiring only changes that differ from the LHCP's current hospital set, whereas the source says the administrator may choose the hospitals to assign, not that authorization depends on the requested set being different from the current set. Repair the property to express permission for the administrator's requested/chosen hospital assignment payload without imposing equality or inequality against resource.hospitals.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement, but the proposed reference Cedar still collapses to a generic Administrator/LHCP principal-resource floor and does not explicitly use the schema's context.hospitals hook for the administrator's chosen/requested hospital assignment payload. Prior rejected variants specifically required making this named source boundary explicit without tautologies or invented equality/inequality checks against resource.hospitals.

The atom covers a real, uncovered requirement and adds the material ownership boundary implied by “their password” rather than collapsing to a generic User/User floor. The validated schema can express this boundary directly with principal == resource for requestPasswordChange, and no additional lifecycle, authentication, or conflict boundary is named in the source excerpt for this workflow.

The atom adds a materially useful ownership safety bound for the password-change workflow that is not implied by the approved own-account floor. It is tightly scoped to the existing requestPasswordChange action and User resource, and uses the schema-expressible ownership boundary principal == resource rather than a generic role/type check.

The atom targets a real, uncovered lifecycle requirement: an authenticated session ends when the user logs out. It is not redundant with the approved login or password-change atoms, and it is tighter than a generic User/Session floor because it scopes logout to the session owned by the principal and to sessions that are currently authenticated. The validated schema exposes the relevant ownership and authentication hooks as resource.user and resource.isAuthenticated, and the proposed property uses them.

The atom is a materially useful same-action ceiling complementing the approved logout floor. It makes the source’s session lifecycle and ownership boundaries explicit: logout applies to the user’s own session and to an authenticated session. These boundaries are represented directly in the schema via resource.user and resource.isAuthenticated, and the atom is not merely a principal/resource type restatement.

The atom covers a distinct lifecycle action from the already-approved logout atoms: closing the application. It is tightly scoped to the source requirement's authenticated-session boundary by requiring the session to belong to the principal and to be authenticated. The validated schema exposes closeApplication and Session.isAuthenticated/resource.user hooks, so the proposed floor is materially useful and not merely a generic User/Session permission.

The atom is a materially useful ceiling complement to the already-approved closeApplication floor. It is not merely restating schema types: it adds the lifecycle/authentication and ownership boundaries exposed by the schema, requiring the session to belong to the acting user and to be authenticated. These boundaries are supported by the source phrase tying application close to an authenticated session ending when the user closes the application, and no stricter approved closeApplication ceiling already covers it.

The atom covers a real, uncovered administrative floor from the source requirement. The action is specifically scoped to setting the inactivity period length on SystemConfiguration, and there is no additional named authorization boundary in the excerpt beyond Administrator authority over that configuration action. It is not implied by any approved atom and is not merely a duplicate.

The atom covers a real, uncovered patient capability and adds the necessary ownership boundary by requiring the Patient principal to view their own Patient resource. The action itself is scoped to past and designated LHCPs, and the schema represents those relationships on the Patient resource, so the proposed floor is tightly aligned with the source requirement rather than a generic Patient/Patient permission.

The atom adds a materially useful same-action ceiling that is not redundant with the approved floor: the floor ensures patients can view their own past/designated LHCPs, while this ceiling prevents access to other patients' corresponding provider lists. The ownership boundary is named in the source through the repeated patient-relative wording and is directly expressible in the schema via principal == resource for Patient resources.

The atom captures a real uncovered provider-list capability and includes the key ownership boundary that the patient may add providers only to their own provider list. The provider payload is represented by the existing context.provider hook, and LHCPs are covered through the schema's LHCP-in-HCP hierarchy. The search-by-name/specialty/optional-zip workflow should be covered by a separate searchProviders atom rather than blocking this addProviderToList ownership property.

The atom captures a real ownership boundary from the phrase "their provider list" that is not implied by the Patient/Patient principal-resource typing and is not covered by the approved floor. The schema exposes the boundary directly as resource Patient equality with principal, and the proposed ceiling is tightly scoped to the addProviderToList action while preserving the provider type condition.

The atom covers an uncovered, materially useful workflow: a Patient may designate an LHCP as that patient's DLHCP. It includes the named ownership boundary from the source by requiring principal == resource, and uses the existing context.lhcp hook for the LHCP being designated. Although context.lhcp is typed by the schema, the self-record boundary makes this more than a generic principal/resource floor.

The atom captures a material patient-specific ownership boundary from the source phrase "for that patient" and is not implied by the schema's Patient principal/resource typing or by the already-approved floor. The schema exposes the needed hooks via the Patient resource identity and context.lhcp, and the ceiling is a useful same-action complement preventing designation on another patient's record.

The atom covers a distinct, still-unapproved source capability: a patient may undesignate an LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient. It is not a duplicate of the approved designate floor/ceiling atoms because it uses the separate undesignateDLHCP action. The proposed floor is tightly scoped to the patient acting on their own patient record and uses the schema's context.lhcp hook to preserve the LHCP/DLHCP designation boundary named in the requirement.

The atom covers a real, not-yet-approved ownership ceiling for the undesignateDLHCP action. It is not merely restating principal/resource types because it adds the source-named 'for that patient' boundary via principal == resource and preserves the LHCP designation target via context.lhcp is LHCP. The schema exposes the needed hooks, and the property is materially distinct from the already-approved floor and from the analogous designate ceiling.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and correctly uses the AccessLog.patient ownership boundary, but the source access-log requirement also names a date-period boundary: the patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period. The validated schema exposes this through viewAccessLog context.beginDate and context.endDate, so the property should be repaired to make the requested access-log period explicit rather than only stating the ownership floor.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped: it covers the previously missing access-log ownership and chosen-period boundaries using the schema's AccessLog.patient, context.beginDate, and context.endDate hooks. It is not a duplicate of an approved atom and does not collapse to a generic Patient/AccessLog floor.

This is a materially useful ceiling counterpart to the approved access-log floor. It captures the named ownership boundary that a patient views the patient's own access log and uses the schema-exposed beginDate/endDate context for the access-log period, preventing policies from also allowing other patients' logs or an invalid requested period. It is not merely a principal/resource type restatement and is not implied by the approved floor alone.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped to an uncovered patient medical-record access requirement. It includes the named ownership boundary via resource.patient == principal and the explicitly mentioned family-history boundary via resource.includesFamilyHistory. It is not merely a generic Patient/MedicalRecord type floor and is not implied by any approved atom.

The atom captures a materially distinct, uncovered source requirement: personal representatives may view medical records, including family history, for patients they represent. It is not implied by the approved patient-own-record atom, and it uses the schema-exposed ownership and representation boundaries via resource.patient and resource.patient.personalRepresentatives. The family-history condition is also explicit and aligned with the cited source excerpt.

The atom adds a materially useful same-action ceiling for an approved medical-record access capability by enforcing the source’s named ownership/representation boundary: patients may view only their own records, and personal representatives may view only records of patients they represent. This is not merely a schema type restatement and is not implied by the existing floor atoms. The schema exposes the required boundary through MedicalRecord.patient and Patient.personalRepresentatives, and the proposal uses those hooks directly. Omitting includesFamilyHistory from the ceiling is appropriate because family history is content included within medical records, not a limiting ownership boundary for all viewMedicalRecord authorization.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped to an uncovered category-specific requirement under the separate seeRecordHealthInformation action. It uses the schema's ownership boundary for the patient's own record, the context.informationCategory hook for personal health information, and the resource.hasPersonalHealthInformation hook for records that contain that category. It is not merely a principal/resource type restatement and is not implied by the approved viewMedicalRecord atoms, which cover a different action and general medical-record/family-history access.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped: it covers the still-unapproved ceiling for seeRecordHealthInformation, uses the source-named ownership/representation boundary, and constrains access to the three named information categories with the schema's existing category and record-contains hooks. It is not redundant with the approved viewMedicalRecord ceiling because it applies to a distinct action and finer-grained health-information category access.

The source requirement describes a real, uncovered search capability, but the proposed atom collapses to a generic Patient/ProviderSearch principal-resource floor and does not make the named search-criteria boundary explicit: searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code. The validated schema already exposes these as ProviderSearch.name, ProviderSearch.specialty, and optional ProviderSearch.zipCode, so repair the atom to scope the floor to provider-search requests using those criteria rather than only restating the action's principal/resource types.

The atom covers a real provider-search requirement that is not already approved, and it repairs the prior generic search proposal by explicitly using the schema-exposed search criteria boundaries: ProviderSearch.name, ProviderSearch.specialty, and optional ProviderSearch.zipCode. It is tightly scoped to the Patient searchProviders floor and does not omit a named source boundary that is representable in the validated schema.

The atom covers a materially useful positive permission that is not already approved: personal representatives must be able to see personal health information for patients they represent. It is tightly scoped to the source boundaries exposed by the schema: represented-patient ownership via resource.patient.personalRepresentatives, the specific information category via context.informationCategory, and the record-containing-that-category condition via resource.hasPersonalHealthInformation. The approved ceiling restricts this action but does not provide the corresponding floor for personal representatives.

The atom covers a materially useful positive requirement that is not already provided by the approved personal-health-information floor or by the category ceiling. It is tightly scoped to the named source boundaries: patient principal, own medical record ownership, immunizations category, and records that actually contain immunization information.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped: it covers an explicit positive source requirement for personal representatives to see immunizations in represented patients' records, and it includes the named representation boundary, the information-category boundary, and the record-contains-immunizations boundary. It is not merely a principal/resource restatement and is not implied by the approved ceiling, which only bounds allowed access but does not require this represented-record immunization floor.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped. It covers the still-unapproved patient floor for the officeVisitInformation category from the same source sentence that already yielded personal-health-information and immunization floors. It uses the existing schema hooks for ownership, requested information category, and record containment, and it is not merely a principal/resource restatement or implied by the approved ceiling.

The atom is materially useful and tightly scoped: it covers the remaining explicit positive floor for personal representatives seeing represented patients' office-visit information. It includes the named representation/ownership boundary, the office-visit information category boundary, and the resource containment condition. It is not merely restating principal/resource schema types and is not implied by the approved ceiling, which restricts unauthorized access but does not guarantee this positive permission.

The atom captures a real, source-named boundary that is not covered by the approved generic createLHCP floor: a new LHCP must have a specified specialty. The validated schema exposes this boundary through LHCP.specialty, and the proposed property is tightly scoped to Administrator createLHCP on LHCP resources with an explicit non-empty specialty condition rather than merely restating principal/resource types.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and uses the existing context.hospitals payload, but it replaces the source's named 'multiple hospitals' boundary with a weaker nonempty-set proxy. `context.hospitals.containsAny(context.hospitals)` only distinguishes empty from nonempty and does not express that the administrator may assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals. If the intended property is about the chosen/requested hospital payload, repair it without inventing a nonempty-only boundary; if the property must enforce true multiplicity, the validated schema/Cedar hook lacks a cardinality/count boundary for the hospital set.

The atom targets a real uncovered requirement and correctly uses the schema's context.assignsMultipleHospitals hook for the named multiple-hospitals boundary. However, the same source sentence also names the administrator's ability to choose the hospitals, and prior reviews specifically rejected generic or tautological assignment floors that failed to make the requested/chosen hospital set explicit. The validated schema exposes that boundary as context.hospitals, so the property should be repaired to scope the floor to the administrator's chosen/requested hospital assignment payload as well as the multiple-hospitals condition, rather than only checking the boolean multiplicity flag.

The atom targets a real uncovered administrative assignment requirement and correctly includes the multiple-hospitals boundary via context.assignsMultipleHospitals, but the reference Cedar again uses context.hospitals == resource.hospitals. That condition over-constrains the floor to cases where the requested hospital set already equals the LHCP's current hospital set, which can make the assignment a no-op and does not express the administrator's ability to choose the hospitals to assign. Repair the atom to scope authorization to the administrator's requested/chosen context.hospitals payload together with the multiple-hospitals boundary, without imposing equality or inequality against resource.hospitals.
